title: Former US intelligence official claims there is a giant 'UFO base' at the bottom of the ocean
excerpt: Former US intelligence official claims there is a giant 'UFO base' at the bottom of the ocean
content:
mystery

Express newspaper

05/10/2026 22:47

A former US Air Force officer and former intelligence official has made sensational new claims about the existence of a giant underwater structure, which, according to him, is used as a "base of operations" by flying vehicles of non-human origin.

David Grusch , who in 2023 testified under oath before the US Congress about alleged secret UFO programs, recently spoke on Joe Rogan 's podcast , saying that US officials are aware of at least one large structure at the bottom of the ocean.

Grusch did not present public evidence for this claim and did not indicate the location of the facility.

"I will be careful because this touches on sensitive US Navy issues related to underwater operations," he said.

According to Grusch, the structure is extremely large.

"It's clear that there is some kind of base of operations in some places. It's huge. I don't know when it got there... We're talking about the size of several city blocks," he declared.

He added that unidentified objects "enter and exit" this area.

Claims that the information comes from top secret programs

Grusch said his claims are based on classified program documents, video footage and testimony from people who have worked within the US military and government.

However, no verifiable evidence has been published to date proving the existence of the base he described.

American institutions have repeatedly stated that they have found no verified evidence that the unidentified objects reported by military personnel represent extraterrestrial technology.

Grusch did not explain how the military supposedly discovered the underwater structure. He said only that the methods used for tracking are related to national security and therefore cannot be discussed publicly.

According to him, however, American authorities have long monitored activity in the area.

“The Abyss is almost a documentary”

During the interview, Grusch also made an unusual claim related to James Cameron's famous science fiction film "The Abyss" , released in 1989.

In the film, a team working on an underwater platform encounters non-human beings living in a large structure deep in the ocean.

Grusch said that people with experience in the military underwater community had told him that the film was closer to reality than one might think.

"I've known people in the underwater community who would say to me, 'You know, Dave, The Abyss is kind of a docudrama.' And I was speechless," he said during the September 30 episode.

This claim has also not been accompanied by public evidence.

Who is David Grusch?

Grusch served for about 14 years in the US Air Force , before working as an intelligence officer for the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) , the agency that designs and operates reconnaissance satellites for the Pentagon.

From 2019 to 2021, he represented the NRO on the government group investigating unidentified aerial phenomena, known today as UAP – Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena.

He later came forward as a whistleblower, claiming that parts of the US government had kept information about UFOs out of Congressional oversight.

In 2023, Grusch testified before lawmakers that the US had secret, multi-year programs for the recovery and analysis of alleged objects of non-human origin.

Some of these claims, according to him, were based on information received from other people and not on objects he had personally seen.

Similar claims from a US congressman

Grusch's statements about underwater activity resemble those previously made by Republican Congressman Tim Burchett of Tennessee , a member of the House Oversight Committee, who has publicly addressed the issue of UAPs.

Burchett said that US Navy personnel had reported cases of unidentified underwater objects moving at speeds much greater than traditional military vehicles.

He has also spoken of repeated reports from several deep sea areas, which, according to him, could be located in the Atlantic near the Bahamas.

"Naval personnel have told me that they have seen underwater vehicles that were following and moving at hundreds of kilometers per hour, while our technology reaches much less," he stated in an interview.

Neither of these claims have so far been supported by public evidence indicating extraterrestrial origin.

Grusch claims to have seen videos of non-human bodies

During the interview with Rogan, Grusch made another, even stronger claim.

He said he was shown a video of dead bodies, which were allegedly recovered from the wreckage of a non-human flying vehicle.

According to him, the footage was modern and clear, not blurry recordings or old material related to UFO stories from the 1950s.

Grusch claimed that the beings in the video had pale skin, with a blue-to-white hue, and that the bodies were being kept frozen for further analysis.

When Joe Rogan asked him if he thought the video could one day be released as part of an official declassification process, Grusch replied that it was possible.

"There is a lot of audio-visual material. The problem with the current climate is that you have to bring out the physical evidence as well, because trust in the government is very low," he said.

Still no public evidence

Despite Grusch's profile and his testimony before Congress, the claims of a giant underwater base, extraterrestrial-origin craft, and non-human bodies have not been independently verified and have not been supported by publicly available physical evidence.

Reports of unidentified phenomena have been taken more seriously by American institutions in recent years, but the term UAP does not automatically mean extraterrestrial technology. In many cases, objects remain unidentified due to a lack of sufficient data.

For this reason, Grusch's claims continue to be part of a major debate among lawmakers, former intelligence officials, scientists and skeptics - while definitive evidence that would confirm the existence of extraterrestrial technology or life has yet to be made public. /GazetaExpress/
